summary: This bill establishes a grant program to help local governments and other entities create or expand behavioral health crisis response programs that primarily use mental health professionals and paramedics instead of law enforcement.

scores.thoughts: This bill establishes a grant program to fund behavioral health crisis response programs that do not primarily rely on law enforcement. This expands access to mental healthcare services, which falls under the umbrella of public healthcare.

The bill creates a grant program to support behavioral health crisis response, which can be seen as an expansion of services aimed at assisting vulnerable populations experiencing mental health crises, thus expanding the social safety net.
The bill authorizes 'such sums as may be necessary' for fiscal years 2026-2030 to fund a new federal grant program, creating new spending without any specified offsets or revenue measures.

The entire bill establishes and funds a grant program to expand government-supported behavioral health crisis response teams and services as alternatives to law enforcement, directly advancing government action to expand mental health service access.
